title: Solo alto, reading, and transposing for out-of-pitch instruments
summary: Talk about the alto's lead role, how he read music from age twelve, and transposing at speed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How did the alto parts go in that time when you first started?

Solo alto? Yeah. What would you play? You might as well say you play pretty near like you did the trumpet. It's got to lead all the way through almost. Really? That's right. That's right. I don't see that instrument no more. I wonder why they don't use that anymore.
I don't know. A number of the people have missed it. Because they never used that in New Orleans.
And they said they had fine melody possibilities, you know, carrying the lead.
We never had that in New Orleans.
You didn't just hit the off beats like they did in New Orleans. I know in those brass band music you know you see and they just go da da da da da da.

Oh yeah, we eat any kind of thing. We didn't have nothing picked. Oh, we didn't have nothing picked because this is the situation. For instance, somebody wanted something and you didn't have it, you see? And you had it in your head, you see? So all you got to do is just hit it. Oh, I see. That's the way we used to play.
So how old were you when you started on the alto? On the alto I must have been about twelve
years old. And you were faking then? No, I was playing here with the
band, yeah. Yeah, but I thought you could fake then, too, huh? You could read and fake.
Well, no, that time, we didn't fake nothing at all. We just read. We didn't know. We just had to read music. Oh, everybody read. Everybody read, because we were being taught by this fellow Kerry.

Oh, I see. Let me ask you this. Did you ever have to transpose and change keys because some of the instruments were out of pitch? Oh, yeah, we had. Constantly doing that, huh? Sure, we had. So then you had to do it at full speed and transpose, too? That's right. I've often wondered about that because I know with the piano that we heard at Mrs. New Iberia, who was I speaking of a far ago? Chewy? No. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. Fontenay. That's over there. I just wondered because I knew they must have to transpose because everywhere they go many of these instruments would be out of pitch. That's right. Tell me, do you still have your instruments? Do you still?
